LESSON 40 / ADDITIONAL INTERVIEW CONCEPT
Accessible names and descriptions

An accessible name identifies a control; an accessible description provides supplementary
information. Native labels are preferred, with aria-label, aria-labelledby or aria-describedby where
appropriate.
Accessible name එJකෙන් control එකෙ Jමාකෙකේදෙ කියෙනවා. Description එJකෙන් අම+ර J+ාරතුරු Jදෙයි. Native label මුලින් භාවි+ කෙරන්න.
An email field has a label and a helper message.
Email form · Email address (name) · Name: Email · student@example.com · We will send a receipt here. · Description

Read the diagram: The label gives the field its name. aria-describedby points to helper text, which
adds context without replacing the label. Placeholder is not a reliable replacement for a label.
We will send a receipt here.
Expected result: Assistive technology can identify the field and read its helper description.
Interview question: What is the difference between aria-labelledby and aria-describedby?
Answer: The former supplies a name; the latter supplies a description.
Remember: Name = identity. Description = extra help.
Practice: Add an accessible name to an icon-only button.
